steps.what: Open and check the current lesson outline and already prepared teaching materials in {LMS}, confirming the topic and actual class context before instruction.

Instruct students individually and in groups through lectures, discussions and demonstrations, observe actual understanding, answer questions and adjust explanations while supervising safe participation.

tasks.design: Keep instruction with the teacher, using the existing {LMS} materials. No new automation is proposed after separating the small existing material lookup from actual teaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instruction depends on dialogue and direct observation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing lesson access is sufficient; no new enabler is claimed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise misunderstanding and explain a technical idea in another way.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust while making learning and practical participation safe.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the teaching week.

reach.role: Teaching Assistants, Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School, Except Special Education

evidence.claim: Existing learning-system material access does not remove the teacher's live explanation and observation work.

assumptions: Boundary is live instruction and its actual material lookup. Material adaptation is task 6615; equipment presentation support is task 6620. No part of those actions is counted here. Shares are illustrative.

Teacher's existing lesson supplies lesson ID, topic, goals and source-material version. s1 verifies these directly; missing material requires ordinary manual access, counted there. No free generated lesson is assumed.

Native lesson access was considered and is already adequate. After separating lookup, no changed step was established. This statement requires no routine written report, send or record commit; grading and pupil records remain separate tasks, not hidden inside s2. No change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Actual split between instruction and separate record duties
research_questions: Is lesson lookup already a direct native link?

already_counted.description: Material check and all live teaching remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: No software change or additional upkeep.

steps.what: Establish rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among students, considering school policy, the practical classroom and actual pupil needs, resolving conflicts with responsible colleagues.
Write the classroom rules in the existing {LMS} class area and check the completed wording for clarity, consistency with school policy and appropriate class visibility.
outputs: checked final classroom rules and visibility

steps.what: Publish the checked final rules to the verified class area in {LMS}.
inputs: checked final classroom rules and visibility

steps.what: Explain the rules directly with students, discuss examples and answer questions about fair behaviour and practical classroom procedures.
Enforce rules and maintain order through actual supervision, proportionate interventions and individual conversations, responding to the immediate behaviour rather than an automated pupil judgement.
Write any required factual incident entry in the existing pupil-record system {OTHER}, recording the actual observation and response, then check the completed entry and authorised access.
Commit the checked factual incident entry in the existing pupil-record system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Keep rule setting, explanation and enforcement human. Existing {LMS} publication and pupil-record software {OTHER} already handle the separate written rules and actual incident entries; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fair interventions depend on immediate classroom context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native rule and record functions are sufficient.
tasks.still_hard: Respond proportionately while preserving trust and order.
tasks.human_edge: Hear the pupil's perspective and explain the response.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in rule-setting or enforcement duties.

evidence.claim: Native class publication and pupil-record entry can already support classroom rules without automating interventions.

assumptions: Boundary includes rule design, actual rule publication, classroom enforcement and required factual incident entries. Shares are illustrative over this work, not an assertion that every interaction creates an incident. No parent-message or disciplinary-decision workflow is invented.

School policy supplies policy revision and recording criteria. Teacher supplies actual rule wording, class visibility, observed incident, time, response and record access in s1-s2 and s6. Missing facts require direct clarification counted there, not inferred labels.

Native tools were tested conceptually first; after splitting rule writing/publication and incident writing/commit from conversations, no removable double entry was established. All steps retain their time and no new upkeep is introduced.
s2 and s6 contain ordinary checks after the completed content exists; no extra self-approval activity is added. a1 and a2 bind their exact content and visibility, and edits require rechecking.
research_questions: Is there any real duplicate incident entry beyond the current native record?

already_counted.description: Rules, publication, explanation, enforcement and actual record/check/commit remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: No change, so no additional upkeep.

Actual factual incident entry and access checked in s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Writing, publication, actual record work and all classroom interaction remain fully counted; no actual removed action is established.

steps.what: Review actual classroom observations, student work and the source instructional materials to understand varying needs and interests, clarifying uncertainties directly with students or relevant colleagues.

Choose adaptations to teaching methods and materials, specifying the lesson goal, retained technical meaning, practical safety constraints and appropriate language or format without assigning a diagnosis or education level.

Rewrite instructional text and examples in the {LMS} lesson editor for the selected adaptation; use native format controls first, then a bounded draft assistant only for the teacher-specified language rewrite, checking it against the original technical material.

loop.purpose: Draft a specified language adaptation without changing the learning goal or technical constraints
loop.input: Source text and teacher-selected non-identifying adaptation brief
loop.check: Teacher compares each instruction, example and safety qualification with its original and the stated learning goal
loop.stop: At most two drafts; unsupported content or unresolved loss of meaning returns to manual rewriting
loop.why_not_simpler: Native layout and style controls cannot make a meaning-preserving language rewrite

steps.what: Check the complete adapted material and selected class visibility, ensuring the same technical meaning, accessible instructions, valid examples and all practical safety qualifications; edit until the final version is suitable.
outputs: checked final adapted material and visibility

steps.what: Save the checked final adapted material in {LMS}.
inputs: checked final adapted material and visibility

steps.what: Publish the checked adapted material to its verified class audience in {LMS}.
inputs: checked final adapted material and visibility

steps.what: Adapt teaching methods during actual use, trying the selected explanation or demonstration, observing whether the material meets students' needs and interests and revising the approach directly with them.

tasks.design: Use native {LMS} formatting first and a bounded drafting loop for teacher-specified text adaptation. The teacher decides needs and methods, checks the full meaning before separate save/publication steps and retains actual classroom adjustment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meaning-preserving rewrites take time after the teacher selects an adaptation.
tasks.enabler_now: A constrained draft assistant can propose alternate wording for direct source comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Know whether an adaptation helps this student in practice.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise needs through actual interaction and adjust teaching accordingly.

ambition.what: No automatic pupil assessment or level assignment.

tasks.altitude: Less first-draft rewriting with unchanged pedagogical decisions.

evidence.claim: A bounded text-drafting assistant can propose alternate wording, requiring teacher comparison of technical meaning and suitability.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual needs review, adaptation decisions, material rewrite/check/publication and targeted trial of the adaptation. General lesson delivery belongs to task 6610; s7 counts only the additional method adjustment, not that same delivery. Shares are illustrative.

Teacher produces goal, source/version, requested language level, retained terminology, safety qualifications and class visibility in s1-s2. Missing source detail requires original-material reading and direct clarification, counted there. No free structured needs profile or prepared brief is assumed.

No identifiable pupil records or diagnostic details enter the draft loop. Native formatting and existing reusable material are tested first; use the loop only where an actual fresh language rewrite remains. Rejected drafts are manually rewritten within retained s3-s4 effort; if this exceeds it, no saving is assumed.

s4 is the normal completed-material quality check, with no extra self-approval activity. It binds the final content and audience for both requested gates; any edit requires rechecking. Native saves and publication keep full time.
unknowns: Actual rewrite frequency and rejection time
research_questions: Does the rewrite preserve every technical and practical constraint with less total review time?

already_counted.description: Needs review, decisions, retained drafting, complete quality check, actions and classroom adjustment remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Maintain source constraints, review rejected examples and check editor changes.

Same final adapted material and class visibility checked in s4

tasks.short: Use audiovisual equipment to supplement presentations

steps.what: Locate the already selected presentation files and audio-visual resources in {LMS}; configure native lesson resource links to reduce repeated folder navigation, checking the correct version and source.
Set up the actual computers, projector, audio and other demonstration equipment, connecting and testing the devices and arranging physical materials for the presentation.

Preview the actual presentation content and output routing in presentation software {OTHER}, checking readability, sound, playback sections and absence of unintended pupil information before displaying it to the class.

Use computers, audio-visual aids and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations, operating the checked display or playback, timing demonstrations and responding to equipment or visibility problems in the room.

tasks.design: Configure native lesson resource links in {LMS} for repeated retrieval. Keep physical equipment setup, preview and actual presentation operation human; no new content production or automatic classroom broadcast is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Presentation resources may be retrieved repeatedly from different folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lesson links can point to existing selected material.
tasks.still_hard: Make equipment and content usable in the actual classroom.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what students can hear and see and adjust the demonstration.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less retrieval; equipment operation stays the same.

evidence.claim: Native lesson-resource links can reduce repeated retrieval while equipment setup and live presentation remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary is the audiovisual support contribution, not the live subject explanation in task 6610 or material adaptation in 6615. No shared action is counted again. Shares are illustrative. Existing material creation is not credited as a saving.

Teacher's existing presentation plan supplies resource IDs/versions, lesson association, intended playback section and class destination. s1 verifies links and source versions; broken links require manual original-file retrieval counted there. s2-s3 establish actual equipment and output readiness.

Native links precede code. Only repeated file navigation loses time; physical setup, preview and live operation retain full effort. No routine report or manual record commit is required by this statement. s3 is the normal final preview, not an added approval activity; changed content or routing requires another preview before display.
research_questions: Are selected resources already directly linked to each lesson?

already_counted.description: Retained retrieval verification, setup, preview and live equipment operation remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Check resource links and update moved material references.

approvals.approved_version: Actual presentation content, playback section and routing previewed in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 5 less 1 upkeep gives 4. Zero for already linked resources; upper case removes repeated file navigation only.
